activity.notes: The Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867 created the Dual Monarchy, and Franz Joseph was crowned King of Hungary in Budapest on 8 June 1867 while remaining Emperor of Austria. He continued as the common monarch until his death in 1916. ATLAS therefore records a distinct Austria-Hungary sovereign Activity from 1867 to 1916 instead of extending the Austrian Empire polity unchanged through the constitutional reorganization.

sources.title: Franz Joseph I — Die Welt der Habsburger
sources.citation_text: The Habsburg history portal gives Franz Joseph's overall reign as 1848-1916 and identifies the 1867 Compromise with Hungary as the creation of the Dual Monarchy.

sources.title: The Austro-Hungarian Dual Monarchy: the coronation of the Hungarian royal couple — Die Welt der Habsburger
sources.citation_text: The Habsburg history portal states that the 1867 Compromise created the Austro-Hungarian Dual Monarchy and records Franz Joseph's coronation as King of Hungary in Budapest in 1867.
